item.title: Savar couple forced to cross neighbour’s roof to leave home
item.description:
An elderly couple in Savar has been forced to climb a 10-12-foot brick wall and cross a neighbour’s rooftop every time they need to leave their home after their access to the road was allegedly blocked by a wall built in front of their main gate.
The couple, who have lived in their home for more than three decades, say they have been facing the ordeal for nearly eight years.
The incident took place in the Nogorchar area of Rajfulbaria under Tetuljhora union in Savar.
Anisur Rahman, originally from Manpasha village in Jhalokathi Sadar, and his wife, Rashida Begum, bought four decimals of land in Rajfulbaria in 1995 and built their home there.
During a recent visit, this correspondent found the couple using a wooden ladder to climb onto a neighbour’s rooftop before making their way outside. At their age, the risky route has made even routine activities, such as going to a hospital or buying essential items, difficult.
Anisur alleged that Aslam, the brother of former union member Ayub, had tried to buy his land for Tk10 lakh during the previous Awami League government.
“I refused to sell the land. Later, Aslam allegedly built a wall in front of our gate, cutting off our access to the road. Since then, we have had to use a ladder and cross a neighbour’s roof to leave our home,” he said.
Anisur said the couple had been using the makeshift route for about eight years.
Rashida said the situation becomes particularly difficult when someone in the family falls ill.
“Taking a sick person to hospital is extremely difficult because we have to cross another person’s rooftop first,” she said.
Aslam was unavailable for comment when this correspondent visited the area.
However, Ziaur Rahman, manager of Aslam’s house, said Aslam had purchased four decimals of land from a person named Reza.
He claimed that Anisur later had a road recorded alongside his property in the BS record. A case has since been filed in court seeking cancellation of the record, he said.
Aman Ullah Aman, MP for Dhaka-2, said he was looking into the matter.
“If the affected family contacts me, I will try to resolve the issue as soon as possible,” he said.
Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khan said the field administration had been instructed to take necessary action.
“If the land has been illegally occupied, action will be taken against those responsible,” she said.

item.title: Bogra leads Rajshahi Board in SSC results
item.description:
Bogra has secured the top position in both the number of GPA-5 achievers and overall pass rate in this year’s SSC (Secondary School Certificate) and equivalent examinations under the Rajshahi Education Board.
A total of 5,900 students from Bogra educational institutions obtained GPA-5, while the district also recorded the highest pass rate, according to results published on Monday.
The overall pass rate in the Rajshahi Board stood at 77.63%, whereas Bogra achieved a district-level pass rate of 83.50%.
Notably, several renowned institutions in Bogra maintained their strong track record of academic excellence.
This year, a total of 180,310 students from eight districts under the Rajshahi Education Board appeared for the SSC examinations.
Of them, 139,983 students cleared the exams, resulting in a board-wide pass rate of 77.63%.
A total of 22,327 students achieved GPA-5, with the highest number coming from Bogra.
These figures were confirmed by Professor Md Ariful Islam, exam controller of the Rajshahi Education Board.
Among the top-performing institutions in Bogra, Bogra Zilla School led the way, with 217 out of 220 students securing GPA-5 and a 100% pass rate.
Bogra Government Girls' High School also achieved a 100% pass rate, with 237 out of 250 students earning GPA-5.
Biam Model School and College had 473 examinees, all of whom passed, and 399 obtained GPA-5. At Bogra Cantonment Public School and College, all 371 students passed, with 342 achieving GPA-5. The Armed Police Battalion Public School and College saw 347 students appear in the exam, all of whom passed, and 286 attained GPA-5.
RDA Laboratory School and College had 242 examinees, 149 of whom achieved GPA-5, with a pass rate of 99.59%.
At TMSS Public School, all 158 students passed, with 98 securing GPA-5.
Bogra Yakubia Girls' High School and College reported a 100% pass rate among its 244 students, with 169 earning GPA-5.
Mustafizur Rahman, principal of Biam Model School and College in Bogra, credited the consistent success of the institution to the collective efforts of students, teachers, staff, and guardians.
He expressed hope for even better results in the future.
Colonel Md Masud Rana, principal of Bogra Cantonment Public School and College, also acknowledged the vital role of the institution’s key stakeholders—including the chief patron, governing body chairman and members, teachers, and guardians—in achieving such outstanding results.
He also expressed optimism about maintaining this performance in the years to come.

item.title: Land acquisition delays keep two bridges unusable in Dumuria
item.description:
Two bridges in Dumuria upazila of Khulna were completed three years ago, but remain unusable as their approach roads have not been built due to unresolved land acquisition disputes.
The situation has left thousands of residents, including students, facing serious difficulties in travelling between villages on either side of the bridges.
According to the Dumuria upazila engineering office, construction of the 65-metre Kulati Bridge over the Mora-Bhadra River began in 2018 at a cost of Tk 4.64 crore to improve communication between Badurgacha and Kulati villages in Gutudia Union. The bridge was completed within three years.
However, disputes over ownership of land needed for the approach road emerged from the beginning. Despite the issue remaining unresolved for nearly eight years, the approach road has yet to be constructed, leaving the bridge largely unused.
Construction of the 84-metre Gajendrapur Bridge over the same river also began around the same time at a cost of Tk 4.84 crore to improve communication between Sahas and Sharafpur unions. The bridge was completed three years ago, but its approach road remains unfinished for the same reason.
Meanwhile, similar land acquisition complications have affected two other major bridges currently under construction in the upazila.
A 750-metre bridge over the Sharafpur-Gaoghara River is being built at a cost of Tk 119.52 crore, while a 461-metre bridge over the Kadamtala-Madartala River in Shovna Union is being constructed at a cost of Tk 67.55 crore. Land acquisition for their approach roads is also yet to be resolved.
Ram Prasad Mondal, one of the landowners whose property is needed for the Kulati Bridge approach road, said several investigations had been conducted into the issue, but 15-16 landowners on both sides of the bridge had yet to receive compensation.
Uttam Sarkar, a teacher at Kulati Secondary School, said residents had previously used a bamboo footbridge to cross the river. After it was removed following construction of the new bridge, local residents had to build bamboo stairs at their own expense to access the bridge.
“People have no choice but to take considerable risks to cross the bridge,” he said.
Mashiur Rahman Liton, a BNP leader, said the Gajendrapur Bridge was now being used to dry paddy instead of for transportation because it had no approach road.
He said communication between the two unions could be disrupted completely if the old bridge collapses.
Monoranjan Das, acting chairman of Sharafpur Union Parishad, said the failure to open the bridge three years after its completion was causing significant hardship for residents and hurting local businesses.
Dumuria Upazila Engineer Darul Huda said he had been trying to resolve the issue for the past two years, but the land acquisition process remained stuck in bureaucratic complications.
“We cannot construct the approach roads until the land acquisition issue is resolved,” he said.
Dumuria Upazila Nirbahi Officer Sabita Sarker said the administration was making efforts to resolve the issues involving the Kulati and Gajendrapur bridges.
Khulna-5 MP Ali Asgar Lobby said effective measures would be taken soon to make the two bridges operational.

item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal-1 has summoned Maj Gen (retd) Ziaul Ahsan to appear before it on August 27 in a crimes-against-humanity case over the disappearance of BNP leader and current Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed in 2015.
The tribunal passed the order on Monday after hearing a prosecution petition seeking proceedings against the former army officer in the case.
The prosecution later said it had filed an application against Ziaul in connection with Salahuddin's disappearance. The tribunal accepted the application and ordered him to appear on August 27.
Ziaul is currently arrested in connection with several other crimes-against-humanity cases.
Salahuddin filed a complaint with the Chief Prosecutor's Office on June 3, 2025, accusing seven people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, over his disappearance.
The other accused are former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former inspector general of police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed, former IGP AKM Shahidul Haque, former Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) commissioner Asaduzzaman Mia, Maj Gen (retd) Ziaul Ahsan and former head of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit Monirul Islam.
Salahuddin, a BNP leader, was allegedly picked up from a house in Uttara, Dhaka, on the night of March 10, 2015.
He was later found by local police in Shillong, Meghalaya, India, on May 11 that year.
After he was arrested in India, authorities filed a case against him under the country's Foreigners Act for allegedly entering India without valid documents.
Salahuddin returned to Bangladesh on August 11, 2024, after spending more than nine years in India. His return followed the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government on August 5, 2024, during the mass uprising.

item.title: IDLC, Friendship sign MoU to establish solar village in Gaibandha
item.description:
IDLC Finance PLC and Friendship NGO have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish a solar village in Mollar Char, Gaibandha, Rangpur.
The project aims to provide clean energy, solar-powered irrigation facilities and community infrastructure in the remote, climate-vulnerable char area.
The MoU was signed by M Jamal Uddin, CEO and Managing Director of IDLC Finance PLC, and Runa Khan, Founder and Executive Director of Friendship, at IDLC Finance's corporate head office in Gulshan, Dhaka.
The initiative will be implemented during 2026-2027 as part of IDLC's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) commitment under its Environment and Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation pillar.
The project includes a 30 kWp solar-powered micro-grid system, 2 solar irrigation pumps, prepaid energy meters for 70 households, 1 electric husking machine, 2 electric threshers and refrigeration support for local shops and pharmacies.
It will also include capacity-building initiatives for 10 local para-solar technicians to support community-based operation and maintenance.
Through Friendship Farmer Clubs and Sustainable Economic Development Hubs, para-solar technicians will receive training, while additional electricity will create opportunities for climate-smart agriculture.
The initiative is expected to directly benefit approximately 315 people, including farmers who will receive solar-powered irrigation across 10 acres of land, households receiving electricity and community members using shared electric farming machinery.
“The lack of reliable electricity and modern irrigation infrastructure at Mollar Char has been significantly constraining agricultural productivity by increasing production costs. It is also limiting economic opportunities. I hope our partnered efforts with Friendship for the Solar Village project will make a difference to the community and uplift their lives in the long term,” said M Jamal Uddin, CEO and Managing Director of IDLC Finance PLC.
Runa Khan, Founder and Executive Director of Friendship, said: “On the chars, resilience is built through practical solutions that give people greater control over their own lives. Friendship's micro-grid with solar irrigation pumps brings this reality to fruition. Reducing farming costs by 1/3, bringing safety to the community and reliable energy into homes. Uplifting livelihoods and turning clean technology into opportunity, dignity and greater economic security.”
Most households in the char primarily depend on agriculture and cultivate leased land. Although some households have basic home solar power, it is mostly incapable of powering all household appliances simultaneously.
As the community remains beyond the reach of the national electricity grid, landless farmers have to rely on diesel-powered irrigation, resulting in higher seasonal and transportation costs and operational inefficiencies.
The integrated model aims to provide households with renewable energy while supporting sustainable livelihoods.
The project builds on Friendship's experience in renewable energy interventions, including the development of Bangladesh's first solar micro-grid and the operation of 7 solar villages across Kurigram and Gaibandha.
The Mollar Char solar village project is another addition to this work. Through the partnership, IDLC Finance and Friendship aim to expand renewable energy access for vulnerable communities while addressing energy access, agricultural productivity, livelihoods and climate resilience in remote char communities.

item.title: Pori Moni drug case: Charge hearing deferred to Sept 29
item.description:
A Dhaka court has set September 29 for the hearing on charge framing against film actress Pori Moni and two others in a drug case filed with Banani Police Station.
The hearing was scheduled for Monday at the court of Judge Md Robiul Alam of Dhaka Special Judge Court-10. However, Pori Moni’s lawyer Nilanjana Rifat (Surabhi) sought an adjournment.
In her petition, the lawyer said Pori Moni could not appear in court as her child had developed a fever after receiving a vaccination. She also cited her child’s birthday as another reason for her absence.
The court granted the time petition and fixed September 29 for the next hearing, the lawyer said. In 2021, Pori Moni made headlines after accusing a businessman of attempting to rape her. Days later, on August 4 that year, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) raided her residence and said it had recovered alcohol and drugs. She was subsequently arrested and charged in a drug case. She was released after spending about a month in jail.
On October 4 that year, CID Inspector Kazi Golam Mostafa, the investigation officer in the case submitted a charge sheet against Pori Moni and two others.
On January 5, 2022, the court framed charges against the three accused and ordered the trial to begin. The other two accused are Pori Moni’s manager Ashraful Islam Dipu and her maternal uncle Kabir Hossain Howlader. RAB-1 official Majibor Rahman, the complainant in the case, has already begun testifying before the court.
After the charges were framed, Pori Moni filed a petition with the High Court seeking the cancellation of the case. On March 1, 2022, the High Court issued a rule and stayed proceedings against her for three months.
The higher court later ordered that the charges be framed afresh in the case.

item.title: Dinesh Trivedi: We don't only share border, we also share dreams
item.description:
Describing his first meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as fruitful, Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Monday said Bangladesh and India not only share a border but alsoP share dreams.
"We are looking forward. Our invitation is there in place. We are positive that if the two leaders meet together, there will be discussion. There will be issues in democracies. It's not democracy if there is no issue. But there is only one people's issue, which is good relations. It's a win-win situation if there is a good relationship," he told reporters when his attention was drawn to the outcome of the meeting.
The high commissioner said they met more as public figures.
"I am not a diplomat. It's like people's representative to people's representative. I am very delighted that we have met. I didn't feel that I met him for the first time. Very good, very humble, on the ground, what will be the discussion - people-to-people relations," said the Indian diplomat.
The envoy said there is no issue that cannot be solved. "I can tell you this confidently."
He, however, did not comment when asked whether the prime minister would be attending the BRICS Summit's outreach session next month in New Delhi.
The high commissioner also met Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed after his meeting with the prime minister.
Despite brief tensions that surfaced between Dhaka and New Delhi following former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s recent speech in New Delhi, Bangladesh and India are heading toward renewed engagement, signaling their intent to take bilateral relations forward constructively.
Dinesh Trivedi, who submitted his credentials to the President on June 25, discussed issues of mutual interest in two separate meetings on Monday.
Ahead of his meeting with the prime minister, the high commissioner met Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman at state guesthouse Padma on Sunday afternoon as both sides continue efforts to engage constructively.
Dhaka has reaffirmed its "Bangladesh First" policy and underscored its commitment to a forward-looking and mutually respectful relationship with India based on sovereign equality, mutual trust and understanding, and mutual benefit.
Bangladesh and India have more than forty bilateral mechanisms covering areas including water, trade, border management and consular issues.
India is willing to engage with the government in Bangladesh by gradually reactivating all the bilateral mechanisms, pursuing a relationship that keeps “people at the center” of everything.
On Sunday, the high commissioner described Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi as people’s persons and expressed optimism that solutions to issues between the two countries could be found if the two leaders meet.
"We all respect him (PM Tarique Rahman) a lot. He speaks from his heart. I listened to his speeches many times…. He is a people’s person, our Prime Minister (Modi), too. I think when two leaders meet, a lot of problems are sorted out. I have full confidence," he told reporters.
The high commissioner said people are united and there will certainly be a solution. "I am very confident. There is nothing negative. Things remain positive."
On August 4, India confirmed that an invitation had been extended to Prime Minister Tarique to attend the BRICS Summit as the BIMSTEC Chair, while a separate bilateral invitation has been in place since February this year.
India will host the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, focusing on global cooperation, trade and sustainable development.
"You would be aware that a formal invitation to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to visit India was extended when he assumed office in February 2026," said Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal during a media briefing in New Delhi.
As far as the BRICS Summit is concerned, he said India has separately extended an invitation to the Bangladesh prime minister in his capacity as the current Chair of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
"The invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner," the MEA spokesperson said.
BIMSTEC comprises seven countries in the Bay of Bengal region - Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
In April last year, Bangladesh assumed the chairmanship of the regional grouping for the next two years, reaffirming its commitment to advancing regional cooperation and development.
"We are reviewing it now. We will take a decision and inform you immediately," Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur told reporters on July 29 when asked about Bangladesh's response to the invitation.
On August 6, High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi met Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood and exchanged views on further strengthening cooperation in the power and energy sectors.
The discussion focused on the importance of cross-border power and energy connectivity as a key pillar of Bangladesh-India economic partnership.
Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to advancing cooperation based on mutual interest and mutual benefit, with a view to enhancing energy security, promoting sustainable development, and supporting the prosperity of the people of both countries.
"We import diesel from India through the pipeline, and we have requested them to supply more," the Energy Minister told reporters after the meeting.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam reiterated that Dhaka wants constructive engagement with New Delhi, noting that the two neighbors have a wide range of bilateral issues requiring continued dialogue.
"We want our relations... because we have many issues with India, many bilateral issues - water, energy, and the border - that need to be resolved through discussion and dialogue," she said on Thursday.
Shama Obaed, however, emphasized that Bangladesh's relationship with India extends far beyond the current issue.
"A country has many aspects to its relationship with another country. We need to have a lot of dialogue with them, and we need to hold discussions. We have cooperation on energy, we have a major issue with them over water, and there are issues on the border - these have to be resolved through discussions," she said.
A mother’s simple request can sometimes spark meaningful change, said the Indian High Commission in Dhaka on Sunday, noting that at his first inspection of the Indian Visa Application Centre, a mother appealed to High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi for a safe play area where children could stay while their parents applied for visas.
Just a few weeks later, her request became a reality, and on Sunday she returned to inaugurate the very play area she had envisioned, along with her child.
“A small initiative, but one that reflects a larger spirit: India delivers. It is these people-centric efforts that bring India-Bangladesh ties to life, a relationship whose strongest foundation is its people,” said the High Commission.

PM Tarique inaugurates three pilot SDG villages
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday inaugurated three pilot Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) villages as part of the government’s initiative to localise the SDGs across Bangladesh.
The villages are Mitingachhari in Kaptai upazila of Rangamati, Pankhali in Dacope upazila of Khulna and Nafanagar in Bochaganj upazila of Dinajpur.
The prime minister inaugurated the pilot program through a video conference from Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre, where he attended the national conference titled “Navigating Five Year Strategic Framework for Achieving SDGs: Policy, Partnership and Priorities.”
During the virtual inauguration, the prime minister connected with representatives of the three selected villages.
“We have seen that three villages are connected with us online. These three are SDG villages, meaning all the plans related to the SDGs will be implemented here,” said the prime minister.
He formally declared the inauguration of the three pilot SDG villages.
Tarique Rahman said a range of programs including Family Cards, Health Cards and Farmers’ Cards, loans for small and medium enterprises, school uniforms, madrasa-based education, renewable energy, village tourism, blue employment, “One Village, One Product”, tree plantation, canal excavation and eco-tourism will be implemented on a pilot basis in the three villages.
He said the government will monitor the impact of the programs and, based on their success, plans to expand the model to other villages across the country, Tarique said.
The prime minister expressed hope that the SDG Village initiative would become an internationally recognised development model demonstrating how the government’s election pledges could be translated into practical programmes at the grassroots level.
The General Economics Division (GED) of the Bangladesh Planning Commission and the Governance Innovation Unit (GIU) of the Prime Minister’s Office jointly organised the national conference.
Under the SDG Village Pilot Program, the government is developing the three villages as models for localising the Sustainable Development Goals and implementing SDG-related initiatives at the grassroots level.

item.description:
The prosecution on Tuesday presented a phone conversation in which former state minister for information Mohammad Ali Arafat allegedly threatened to shut down television channels if they broadcast footage or images of clashes during the July Mass Uprising.
The conversation was presented on the fourth day of arguments in the case against seven accused, including former road transport and bridges minister and Awami League general secretary Obaidul Quader, over crimes against humanity committed during the uprising.
The International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Chairman Justice Md Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, began hearing the prosecution's arguments on Monday.
During the hearing, a recording of a conversation between Quader and Arafat was presented to the tribunal.
In the conversation, Quader is heard saying: “Those who do not listen, strict action must be taken against the TV channels…”
Arafat replied: “We shut down one or two yesterday. I have told them today as well that those who do not listen should be shut down immediately.”
Quader then said: “They should not report any clashes today.”
Arafat replied that channels showing footage or images of clashes would be declared “enemy of the state” and shut down permanently.
He also said arrangements had been made through Bangabandhu Satellite to monitor television channels and instructed that any channel showing images of clashes be shut down immediately.
Arafat further told Quader that he had given blanket permission to take such action without seeking his approval and that the channels should not be restored without his permission.
The prosecution is presenting arguments in the case against seven accused.
Besides Quader, the accused are banned Awami League joint general secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim; former state minister for information Mohammad Ali Arafat; Jubo League president Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and general secretary Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil; and banned Chhatra League president Saddam Hossain and general secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.

item.title: PM urges Islamic scholars to stay united to maintain peace, stability
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday urged Islamic scholars (alem-ulema) to work with the government and remain united in the days to come to maintain peace and stability amid various plots to destabilise the country.
Speaking at a views-exchange meeting with Islamic scholars at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Ulum Babunagar Madrasha in Fatikchhari upazila, he said BNP’s political opponents in the 13th parliamentary election are trying to create disorder and spread confusion in the country.
“We saw it in 1991 and 1996. You also saw during the last election that you and we worked together against those who wanted to take the country in a different direction. Over the past few days, they have again been trying to spread various messages of confusion and create disorder,” Tarique said.
He said the government and the alem-uema and Islamic scholars worked together in the past and should continue to do so to keep the country on the right track.
“With the prayers of Huzur [Allama Shah Muhibullah], I want to request that we remain together in the coming days as well,” the prime minister said.
Referring to various demands raised by representatives of Qawmi madrashas, he said Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has already explained some of the issues and that the government would address them gradually.
“We have to understand that many other people also live in this country. We want to build a Bangladesh where its people and children can live well, earn a living and live in peace,” Tarique said.
He said people of different faiths should be able to practise their religions peacefully.
“We will practise our religion, and they will practise theirs. But as most people here are Muslims, we will also take Islam forward and take the country forward, InshaAllah,” the prime minister said.
Explaining his visit to the madrasha, Tarique said he has come mainly to pay his respects and seek the prayers of Allama Shah Muhibullah Babunagari.
He also stressed the need to prevent attempts to create disorder, saying the government has important work to do in improving people’s lives.
“We have to create employment, improve healthcare and education, repair roads, schools and colleges, and fix bridges and culverts in different places,” Tarique said.
The prime minister said peace and stability are essential for attracting both domestic and foreign investment.
“If there is disorder in the country, foreign investors who want to invest here will not come. If there is no disorder, they will invest. Then our children and family members will get opportunities for jobs,” he said.
Tarique said ensuring people’s wellbeing is the government’s responsibility and sought prayers so that the government could fulfil that responsibility. “ Allah has given us this responsibility, and we have formed the government. Pray that we can do something good for the welfare of people,” he said.
The prime minister also warned against attempts to spread confusion and create disorder, saying such activities could undermine the government's efforts to develop the country.
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed also spoke at the meeting.
Tarique had earlier met Hefazat-e-Islam chief Allama Shah Muhibullah Babunagari at the madrasha and enquired about his health.

item.title: Govt mulls launching electric water buses around Dhaka
item.description:
The government is considering launching electric water buses along Dhaka’s 110-kilometre circular waterway as part of efforts to ease the capital’s chronic traffic congestion and develop an alternative public transport network.
Authorities are preparing a comprehensive plan and roadmap to revive passenger and tourist services along the waterway, which runs through the Buriganga, Turag, Shitalakkhya, Balu and Dhaleshwari rivers.
A meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office on July 1 decided to take coordinated measures to launch electric water bus services on the existing circular waterway within a month.
Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation (BIWTC) Chairman ATM Abdul Bari Danny said the authorities are preparing a roadmap to ensure the effective and organized operation of the proposed service.
“We have discussed the matter with the prime minister. We also discussed how the initiative can be operated in an efficient and well-organized manner. We are now preparing a final plan and roadmap, and we hope to operate it successfully in the future,” Danny told Dhaka Tribune.
Asked whether Bangladesh was considering solar-powered or electric vessels similar to those used in developed countries, Danny said electricity supply and utility-related matters fall under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources.
“The utility and electricity-related matters will be dealt with by the Ministry of Power. We cannot comment on this issue,” he said.
The proposed circular waterway stretches 110km around Dhaka, covering five rivers. Of the total route, 63km has a depth of 12 feet, while the remaining 47km has a depth of around eight feet. Conservation dredging is underway along a 10km stretch between Sirnichtek and Ashulia to increase its depth to 12 feet, while the remaining 37km is planned to be deepened gradually.
The waterway connects four river ports—Dhaka, Narayanganj, Tongi and Mirkadim—and has five terminals and nine landing stations, with 45 terminal and landing points in total.
Talking to Dhaka Tribune, Buet transport expert Dr Md Hadiuzzaman said the circular waterway could only succeed if lessons from the previous initiative were addressed through a professionally prepared, integrated and institutionally coordinated plan.
“The new system should provide reliable feeder services, ensure frequent peak-hour operations, regulate vessel and cross-river traffic, and improve river water and environmental conditions,” he said.
The government is also looking to involve private operators in reviving the waterway.
At a July 9 meeting at the Ministry of Shipping, authorities decided to hold discussions with private entrepreneurs interested in operating commercial public transport on the Gabtoli-Sadarghat route.
BIWTA was asked to consult stakeholders and interested entrepreneurs and determine the next course of action.
At another meeting on July 14, BIWTA discussed high-speed launches and speedboats, passenger catamarans and tourist vessels with interested owners and operators.
Participants stressed the need to free Dhaka’s surrounding rivers from encroachment and pollution, establish modern landing stations, improve road connections and ensure adequate public transport links. Passenger safety was also identified as a priority.
Professor Dr Ainun Nishat, adviser at the Centre for Climate Change and Environmental Research, said Dhaka’s inland waterways still have significant potential to ease traffic congestion.
He called for greater private-sector involvement, saying the government should focus on regulation, monitoring and accountability rather than directly managing every aspect of the system.
Nishat also criticised what he described as “projectitis” in Bangladesh’s development administration.
“Projectitis is a major problem in our development system. Ministries often become more interested in taking up projects than actually getting the work done. Once this unnecessary project-driven approach stops, real development can begin,” he said.
He said reviving waterways does not necessarily require mega projects, but rather targeted dredging, correction of sharp bends and regular maintenance.
Water bus services were launched on the Badamtoli-Gabtoli route on August 28, 2010 and the Narayanganj-Tongi route on November 22, 2014. Both services were eventually suspended due to financial losses—in September 2019 and March 2020 respectively.
A total of 12 water buses were constructed at a cost of Tk9.20 crore. According to BIWTC data, they generated Tk2.52 crore in revenue against expenditure of Tk37.87 crore, resulting in a loss of Tk35.35 crore.
The official assessment cited shorter road travel times, Buriganga pollution, traffic congestion around Sadarghat, poor connectivity to landing stations and inadequate infrastructure among the reasons for the service’s failure. Sand-carrying vessels also prevented water buses from maintaining their expected speed.
River pollution remains a major challenge. A recent BIWTA survey identified 424 outlets discharging liquid waste into rivers surrounding Dhaka, including 244 associated with privately owned factories and industrial establishments.
Authorities have decided to identify pollution points and ensure proper collection and disposal of waste generated by vessels.
Nishat said Dhaka’s waterway network must also be redesigned in line with changing transport technologies.
“We are entering the era of electric vehicles and modern transport technologies. We cannot build a new transport system with old ideas. Long-term planning, efficient management and private-sector expertise are essential to make Dhaka’s waterways viable,” he said.
The government is also considering smaller and more frequent vessels to reduce passenger waiting times.
The circular waterway already has 20km of completed walkway, while another 52km is under construction with 92% progress. A further 100km has been proposed.
Authorities have installed 6,320 boundary pillars against a target of 7,100. Between 2009 and 2024, 17,829 illegal structures were removed under Dhaka River Port, recovering 519.04 acres of riverbank land. Another 6,963 illegal structures were removed under Narayanganj River Port, recovering 316.06 acres.
The success of the new initiative will ultimately depend not merely on putting electric vessels on the water, but on integrating waterways with road transport, ensuring reliable landing facilities, maintaining navigability, controlling pollution and providing an affordable and efficient service.

item.title: IRI survey: BNP gains public favour as Jamaat loses ground
item.description:
Public attitudes towards Bangladesh’s major political parties have shifted since last year, with the BNP gaining favour while Jamaat-e-Islami has lost ground, according to the latest nationwide survey by the International Republican Institute (IRI).
The June 2026 survey shows that 57% of respondents hold a favourable view of the BNP, up from 51% in October 2025.
The increase gives the party the highest favourability among the major political forces measured in the survey.
Jamaat-e-Islami, meanwhile, moved in the opposite direction. Its favourability fell to 48%, down from 53% in October last year.
The findings point to a changing political landscape following the February 2026 national parliamentary election.
The National Citizen Party (NCP), which emerged from the political realignment following the July 2024 uprising, remains further behind the two established parties.
Its favourability stands at around 37%, little changed from the previous survey.
The Awami League continues to face the most difficult public perception among the major parties surveyed.
Only around 22% of respondents expressed favourable views of the party, while roughly 72% viewed it unfavourably.
IRI asked respondents whether they strongly or somewhat liked or disliked nine political parties, including the BNP, Jamaat, NCP, Islami Andolan Bangladesh, Awami League and Jatiya Party.
The latest findings are particularly significant because they capture public attitudes several months after the February election, providing an early indication of how the country’s political forces are being perceived in the post-election environment.
The survey was conducted between May 16 and June 24 among 5,000 adults across all 64 districts. IRI said the nationally representative survey has a margin of error of ±1.7 percentage points.

item.title: ‘We were left like nomads for 40 hours at Rome airport’
item.description:
Bangladeshi passengers on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Toronto endured a nearly 40-hour ordeal at Rome airport after a technical problem grounded their flight, with many claiming they were left stranded in the airport lounge due to visa restrictions.
“We spent 40 hours like nomads. Eight hours were spent inside the aircraft. We were then taken to the airport lounge and told we would be taken to a hotel. But passengers holding US and Canadian passports were taken to hotels, while we, the Bangladeshi passport holders, were left in the lounge,” passenger Shahjahan Alam said after arriving in Dhaka.
The flight landed in Dhaka at 12:24pm on Sunday, and passengers began disembarking around 1:30pm, many visibly exhausted.
“They did not value our passports at all. We could not even eat the food they provided. Overall, we spent nearly two days like nomads,” Shahjahan said. Another passenger, Anika, said they learned about the technical problem after three hours.
“We were kept inside the aircraft for another five hours before being allowed to disembark. An airline official later came and apologised,” she said. Anika said Bangladeshi passport holders were kept in the lounge while US and Canadian passport holders were accommodated in hotels.
“We spent 40 hours sitting on chairs. Biman and our embassy could have arranged accommodation for us as well. They even offered visas on arrival, but due to negligence by officials, we had to suffer so much,” she said.
Passenger Shafayat Hossain urged the government to strengthen the Bangladeshi passport.
“As there is a new government and everything is being renewed, we do not want to see the old faces at Biman and the embassy. Still, we thank the government for bringing us back,” he said.
Dhaka University teacher Sayem Rana also criticised the handling of the situation.
“What is the point of reporting on Biman? Where was the coordination? How could we spend so many hours sitting on chairs? We suffered tremendously, yet no one spoke up,” he said.
Mahmuda Talukdar, another passenger, said she was accommodated at a hotel because she held a Canadian passport.
“I was spared the ordeal because I had my young daughter with me. But those who remained at the airport suffered greatly,” she said.
Passengers said the ordeal was particularly difficult for elderly people and children, who had to sit on chairs or sleep on the floor. They urged Biman to improve its services, warning that the national flag carrier could face serious consequences if such problems continue.
Biman flight BG306 departed Toronto for Dhaka on Thursday with 259 passengers. It made a scheduled stop at Rome airport for refuelling, where a technical problem was detected.
After an eight-hour effort failed to resolve the problem, the flight was cancelled and passengers were disembarked. Biman authorities subsequently arranged accommodation for some passengers at hotels and others in the airport lounge.
An engineering team carrying the necessary parts and equipment arrived in Rome at around 11:15pm Bangladesh time on Saturday. The team repaired the aircraft, making it fit for flight.
As the aircraft remained grounded for an extended period and many passengers were unable to leave the airport due to visa restrictions imposed by Italian immigration authorities, they were forced to remain at the airport.
Passengers alleged that they were kept inside the aircraft for nearly eight hours after landing in Rome before being informed about the technical problem. Several children, elderly passengers and those who were ill reportedly became unwell during the prolonged wait.

MA Kashem has been re-elected as chairman of the board of directors of Southeast Bank PLC.

MA Kashem is founder chairman and sponsor director of Southeast Bank PLC.
He is a member & former chairman of board of trustees, North South University and a founder life member of NSU Trust Foundation.
He has served as its four times chairman and was also chairman of NSU Foundation’s Endowment Committee several times. He is the chairman of Rose Corner (Pvt.) Limited.

He was the president of Sahic Trust (Society for Assistance to Hearing Impaired Children), the only voluntary organization rendering health care assistance of the ear, nose and throat services to destitute and poor patients. He is the life member of Sahic.
Kashem is an eminent industrialist, renowned patron of education, distinguished philanthropist and an active social worker.

item.title: PM urges UNOs to serve people with responsibility, humanity
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday urged Upazila Nirbahi Officers (UNOs) to work with the highest sense of responsibility and humanity for the development of the country and welfare of its people, saying public service is a major trust and blessing for those entrusted with state responsibilities.
“Today we are here, tomorrow we will not be. Let us all try to leave a safe Bangladesh for the next generation, where everyone can live a little better,” he said. The prime minister is speaking at a meeting with UNOs from different upazilas at his office in Tejgaon, said a release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
Describing field-level officials as a bridge between the government and the people, he said an upazila where an UNO is posted may not be his or her own, but it is still a part of Bangladesh and its people should be treated like their own. “If we want to put this small country in order, we all have to work together,” he said.
Tarique Rahman also urged the UNOs to play a more active role in raising public awareness, saying every social problem cannot be solved simply by making or enforcing laws.
He stressed the need for stronger local initiatives to protect the environment.
The prime minister noted that Dhaka has long remained among the world’s most polluted cities, but said recent improvements are a positive sign that should be built upon.
He urged UNOs to encourage people and local authorities to plant more trees. “If officials motivate people who already want to plant trees, an individual who plants 10 trees could be encouraged to plant 50.”
Tarique Rahman also asked the field administrators to promote sports at the local level, saying sports help young people develop discipline and positive habits. He said sports events need not be limited to national occasions such as Victory Day or Independence Day and could be organised around any meaningful local occasion.
The prime minister expressed concern over what he described as a decline in compassion and humanitarian values in society.
He suggested that UNOs visit schools and help raise children’s awareness about humanity, compassion and care for animals and nature. He said such values, once taught through family, society and religious practices, have weakened over time.
Tarique Rahman said efforts are being made to bring them back, including by incorporating lessons on humanity and compassion for animals at the primary level.
At the meeting, he praised and thanked UNOs from 83 upazilas for completing canal re-excavation projects and returning surplus funds to the government treasury.
During the meeting, UNOs shared the impact of canal re-excavation projects in their respective upazilas, particularly on agriculture, water management and people's daily lives.
They said areas that previously produced two crops a year are now producing three crops following the re-excavation of canals.
Improved drainage and irrigation have also brought positive changes to farming and local water management, the UNOs said.
They also conveyed messages of thanks and gratitude from beneficiaries to the Prime Minister.
Receiving the messages, he said the main objective of re-excavating canals is to restore the traditional riverine character of Bangladesh.
Tarique Rahman warned that the country’s groundwater level is gradually falling, which could create a serious crisis in the future. “We have to prepare from now to face that situation,” he said.
He said the government plans to re-excavate 20,000 kilometres of canals across the country in phases.
The prime minister expects the programme to bring long-term benefits by conserving water, increasing agricultural production, reducing waterlogging and maintaining environmental balance.
He said national development is not limited to infrastructure or economic growth; building humanity, compassion, and a sense of responsibility among people is also an important part of development. “Our main issue is one. Our goal and objective are also one,” he said.

Dhaka-Sylhet Highway blocked over illegal sand extraction
item.description:
Residents of four villages in Ashuganj upazila of Brahmanbaria blocked the Dhaka-Sylhet highway for an hour on Saturday, protesting the illegal sand extraction from the Meghna River and its threat to nearby farmland and settlements.
Residents of Durgapur, Bahadurpur, Sohagpur and Tajpur blocked the highway by burning tyres at Bahadurpur from 11am to noon, triggering a five-kilometre traffic tailback and causing significant suffering for commuters and long-distance passengers.
The protesters alleged that sand is being extracted illegally from the Ashuganj section of the Meghna under the guise of a lease on the Bhairab side of Kishoreganj.
Rana Sikdar and Munabbir Billah, speaking on behalf of the protesters, said the large-scale extraction was accelerating river erosion and putting agricultural land in the surrounding villages at risk.
They also expressed concern over the possible disappearance of Sonampur, a centuries-old settlement that has emerged in the middle of the Meghna in Ashuganj.
The protesters claimed that local residents went to the river on Saturday to stop the sand extraction but were allegedly chased away by the extractors, some of whom were carrying weapons.
They subsequently formed a procession and blocked the highway, demanding the arrest and exemplary punishment of those involved in the illegal sand extraction.
Brahmanbaria reserved women’s seat MP Nadia Pathan Papon joined the protesters and expressed solidarity with their demands. She said she had spoken with the deputy commissioner and received assurances that sand extraction would be stopped within two days.
Papon also said that if anyone affiliated with the BNP was found involved in illegal sand extraction, action would be taken against them.
Following assurances from the authorities, the protesters withdrew the blockade at noon.
Ashuganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Jamal Hossain, Assistant Commissioner (Land) Kazi Rabius Sarwar and Ashuganj police station Officer-in-Charge AKM Shafiqul Alam Chowdhury were present at the scene.
The officials assured the protesters that necessary action would be taken against illegal sand extraction.
Meanwhile, the highway blockade caused a five-kilometre-long traffic congestion stretching from Sohagpur bus stand to Bertala bus stand, leaving thousands of passengers and local commuters stranded.

item.title: Torrential rain, waterlogging cause extensive damage to Aush paddy in Narail
item.description:
Prolonged rainfall and persistent waterlogging have caused extensive damage to Aush paddy in large areas of Narail district, leaving hundreds of farmers facing heavy financial losses.
Local farmers blamed the situation on blocked natural drainage routes, unplanned fish enclosures and the filling up of canals and drainage channels due to poor maintenance.
They fear the total financial losses from the crop damage will run into several crores of taka.
During a visit to several low-lying areas, including Amadar, Andharkota and Kuchiabari bills in Lohagara upazila, fields were found submerged under chest-deep water.
Instead of ripening paddy, the fields were covered with water lilies and other aquatic weeds, while groups of ducks were seen roaming through the waterlogged farmland.
Affected farmers said the low-lying lands are particularly suitable for the local water-tolerant variety of Aush paddy known as “Ratul Aush.” The variety can grow rapidly as water levels rise.
Farmers had expanded cultivation of the variety this year after obtaining good yields and prices in previous years amid moderate rainfall.
Apart from Lakshmipasha, Ratul Aush was cultivated in more than 50 bills across different unions of the district, including Bangram, Naldhi, Kotakol, Kalabaria, Baiashona, Pohardanga, Khashial, Maijpara and Sekhati.
However, record rainfall that began in mid-July suddenly inundated the low-lying farmland.
Farmers said water remained trapped for a prolonged period because unplanned fish enclosures blocked drainage routes, eventually causing the submerged paddy plants to rot.
The farmers demanded immediate removal of illegal fish enclosures, restoration of blocked canals and drains and re-excavation of connecting canals linked to rivers to improve water drainage.
This year, some 9,107 hectares of land have been brought under Aush paddy cultivation, according to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) in Narail.
Although officials have estimated the crop damage to be limited, farmers strongly disputed the assessment.
They said some paddy in relatively higher areas survived, but most of the crops in low-lying areas had rotted, resulting in losses worth several crores of taka.
Muhammad Arifur Rahman, deputy director of the Narail Department of Agricultural Extension, said the agriculture department was coordinating with other relevant government agencies to restore drainage systems and recover canals that have been filled in or disappeared.
“Permanent waterlogging in the low-lying water body areas has become a major threat to agricultural activities,” he said.

Journalist 'assaulted' in police van after filming police beating woman
item.description:
A multimedia reporter for Global Television, Bulbul Hossain, has alleged that police officers assaulted him inside a police van after he filmed them allegedly beating a woman in the capital’s Bijoy Sarani area.
Bulbul has submitted a written complaint to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) commissioner, seeking legal and departmental action against the officers involved.
He submitted the complaint at the DMP headquarters in Ramna on Thursday afternoon.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Saturday, Bulbul said the incident occurred around 5:30pm on August 4 while he was on his way to cover a clash between Islami Chhatra Shibir and BNP activists.
He said that a police van was stuck in traffic near the Bijoy Sarani intersection, with several motorcycles blocking its path. Police officers reportedly got into arguments with some motorcyclists.
At one point, when a woman approached the van, several officers allegedly assaulted her. Bulbul said he began recording the incident in the line of his professional duty. The officers order him to delete the footage.
He alleged that the officers then forcibly took him into the police van and assaulted him after he refused to delete the video despite identifying himself as a journalist.
According to his complaint, the officers repeatedly struck him on the head, threw him to the floor of the van and beat him. He also alleged that one officer pressed a boot against his chest and attempted to suffocate him.
Bulbul said he was eventually able to leave the van after people nearby came forward upon hearing his screams.
He was later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors reportedly found injuries to his head, eye and chest and advised him to take three days of complete rest.
“I have filed a complaint with the DMP. I have been called by Tejgaon Police Station,” Bulbul said.
When contacted, Mahbubur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station, told the Dhaka Tribune that he had not yet been informed about the complaint by the DMP.
“If the complainant brings a copy of the complaint submitted to the DMP commissioner, we will investigate the matter and take appropriate action,” he said.
In his complaint, Bulbul described the alleged assault as an attempt to silence independent journalism and a violation of human rights. He urged the authorities to identify the officers involved using video footage and eyewitness accounts and take legal and departmental action against them.

item.title: Biman flight makes emergency landing in Rome
item.description:
A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Toronto to Dhaka made an emergency landing at Rome’s Fiumicino Airport due to a technical issue and remained grounded there for at least six hours, officials said.
A public relations official of Biman Bangladesh Airlines confirmed the development on Friday evening, saying the aircraft was grounded after undergoing technical inspections following the emergency landing.
“The aircraft underwent a technical check after landing. Following an initial inspection, the authorities declared it grounded,” the official said, requesting anonymity.
Around 250 passengers were on board the flight.
The national flag carrier is working to arrange alternative flights, accommodation and meals for the affected passengers, the official added.

item.title: Gas shortage intensifies load shedding in Chittagong
item.description:
The partial resumption of operations at the floating LNG terminal in Moheshkhali of Cox’s Bazar has brought only limited relief to Chittagong, where a prolonged gas shortage continues to disrupt electricity generation and worsen daily load shedding across the region.
The LNG terminal resumed operations after remaining shut for nearly two weeks because of a technical fault. However, the restoration has not been sufficient to meet the region's energy demand.
As a result, households and businesses in Chittagong experience frequent power outages, with many residents reporting five to six hours of load shedding every day. Rural communities are facing even longer interruptions.
According to the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), Chittagong has 28 power plants powered by gas, furnace oil, coal and hydropower. Six of those plants were out of operation on August 3 due to mechanical problems, fuel shortages or scheduled operating patterns.
Although the region's installed generation capacity exceeds 4,600 megawatts, actual production has dropped significantly because gas-fired plants are unable to operate at full capacity.
Official data show that electricity generation reached 2,819.14 MW during off-peak hours and 3,302.60 MW during peak hours on August 3. The BPDB reported electricity demand of 1,352.96 MW during off-peak hours and 1,477.2 MW during peak hours, with load shedding recorded at 65 MW and 62 MW respectively.
Consumers, however, said that the official figures do not reflect the reality on the ground, adding that power cuts have become much more frequent and prolonged.
Residents across the city say repeated outages have disrupted daily life and damaged electrical appliances due to constant voltage fluctuations. In rural parts of Chittagong, some areas are experiencing six to seven hours of power cuts each day, making living conditions increasingly difficult during the hot summer months.
The gas shortage has also forced major government-owned power plants to reduce output. Two 210 MW units at the Raozan power station, with a combined capacity of 420 MW, have remained shut because of inadequate gas supply.
The 225 MW Shikalbaha gas-fired power plant has also scaled back production. Plant officials said full-capacity operation requires about 37 million cubic feet of gas per day, but the facility has recently been receiving only 28 to 30 million cubic feet, limiting electricity generation to around 183-184 MW.
According to Karnaphuli Gas Distribution Company Limited (KGDCL), Chittagong's daily gas demand stands at approximately 350 million cubic feet, while current supply is only 200-220 million cubic feet, leaving a daily shortfall of up to 150 million cubic feet. The deficit has affected residential, commercial and transport sectors in addition to electricity generation.
KGDCL Managing Director Engineer Md Salahuddin said that it will take several more days before gas supply returns to normal.
RPGCL Manager Imtiaz Kamal Chowdhury said one terminal has resumed supplying around 180 million cubic feet of gas per day alongside another terminal supplying about 570 million cubic feet.
Following repairs carried out with the assistance of foreign specialists, gas transmission has resumed gradually. However, authorities acknowledge that restoring full electricity generation and stabilising power supply across the region will take additional time.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Govt working to curb syndicates exploiting students looking to study abroad
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Friday said the government is working to curb unscrupulous syndicates and brokers who exploit Bangladeshi students seeking to pursue higher education abroad by charging them excessive money.
“Unscrupulous syndicates or brokers take advantage of our students, who have to pay extremely high amounts of money to go abroad. The government is obviously aware of the issue and is working on it,” she said.
The state minister said while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day 14th International Education Expo 2026, organized by the Foreign Admission and Career Development Consultants Association of Bangladesh (FACD-CAB), at a city hotel.
This year the fair brought together representatives from 30 countries to provide consultancy services for around 300 world-class educational institutions around the world.
Shama Obaed said the foreign ministry has already opened a migration wing for the first time to address the migration related problems. The sole responsibility of this newly opened wing is to address all sorts of migration related problems.
She urged FACD-CAB and others concerned to help the wing by providing necessary information to contain the unscrupulous syndicates in the student migration process.
“Together, we have to work in a unison way here. We have to work together to bring these broker syndicates under the law. They are unfairly destroying the future of our children (students),” she said.
The state minister said the foreign ministry is ready to cooperate with FACD-CAB to make the migration process more transparent and accountable and to help it provide better services to Bangladeshi students.
She asked FACD-CAB to submit in writing its demands and problems so that the issues could be brought to the attention of the Prime Minister as well as the Foreign Ministry together with other concerned ministries, including the Education, Finance and Home ministries, could fulfill their demands and address the problems.
Shama Obaed stressed the importance of creating a safe and investment-friendly environment in Bangladesh so that students attained overseas education and experiences can return home and contribute to the country's development.
“We certainly want our children to go abroad and study. But at the same time, we need to create a safe, investment-friendly and secure environment in Bangladesh where they can return, invest and become entrepreneurs and thus help the government build the country,” she said.
Describing education as an important instrument of diplomacy, she said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue to encourage educational and research partnerships between Bangladesh and other countries.
Bangladesh's missions abroad can help connect Bangladeshi institutions with international universities, facilitate academic cooperation and support the legitimate interests and welfare of Bangladeshi students.
Referring to the national budget for 2026-2027 fiscal year, the state minister said the government has given the highest-ever allocation to the education sector in the latest budget, reflecting its priority to education.
The International Education fair, a flagship international education event, started at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel, bringing together education consultants, international university representatives, students, and stakeholders under one platform.
Visitors need prior registration to visit the education fair from 10:00am to 8:00pm.
Visitors get scope to interact directly with representatives of universities from different countries and receive guidance on scholarships, financial aid, tuition fees, visa processing and career planning.

item.title: Mir Helal: July Uprising belongs to people, not any group
item.description:
State Minister for Land and Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs, Barrister Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin, said it is both inaccurate and misleading to portray the July-August 2024 mass uprising as the achievement of any single individual or group.
"No one can claim ownership of this mass uprising. It belongs to the 18 crore people of Bangladesh," he said.
He said the true outcome of the mass uprising was realized when the people resolved that they would no longer tolerate oppression and that the authoritarian government had to be removed.
He made the remarks while addressing a discussion titled "Fascism, July Revolution and Today's Bangladesh" as the chief guest at the July Memorial Hall of the Chittagong Press Club on Friday afternoon.
The discussion was jointly organized by the Chittagong Press Club and the Chittagong Metropolitan Union of Journalists (CMUJ).
City BNP Convener Ershad Ullah, MP, and Abu Sufian, MP, among others, addressed the event as special guests.
He said Bangladesh had been heavily burdened by the Awami League's 15 years of misrule, during which BNP leaders and activists were subjected to enforced disappearances, severe torture, and false cases.
He added that people from various professions, including journalists with dissenting views, also faced repression, ultimately leading to the July-August mass uprising as a response to years of oppression.
Mir Helal said the uprising was not intended to bring anyone to state power or government; rather, it was fought to establish Bangladesh as a truly independent and sovereign nation.
Zahidul Karim Kachi, president of the Chittagong Press Club, delivered the welcome address. The discussion was moderated by the club's General Secretary Golam Mawla Murad and Joint Secretary Meah Mohammed Arif.
CMUJ President Mohammad Shah Nawaz presided over the event.
Among others, Chittagong University Vice Chancellor Dr Mohammad Al-Forkan, Premier University Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Nasrul Quadir, Chittagong Development Authority Chairman Engineer Belayet Hossain, Chittagong City BNP Joint Convener MA Aziz, Chittagong District Bar Association President Advocate Tarique Ahmed, Press Club Vice President Mustafa Nayyem, Chittagong Metropolitan Union of Journalists General Secretary Saleh Noman, and Advocate Abdus Sattar, an injured July uprising participant and former president of the Chittagong District Bar Association, also spoke at the program.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Youth to be prepared with proper skills before going to Japan
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education, Bobby Hajjaj on Friday said Bangladeshi youths will be prepared according to international standards through language education, technical skills and technological knowledge considering the demands of the international labor market, including Japan.
He said the government's goal is not only to send manpower abroad, but also to develop skilled, language-proficient and world-class human resources.
The state minister made the remarks at a view-exchange meeting with Bangladeshi students, professionals and community representatives living in Osaka and Kobe at a local community center in Osaka, Japan.
"Bangladesh's youths are our greatest strength. The government is continuously working to develop them with international-standard language education, technical skills and technological capabilities," he said.
If skilled manpower can be created according to the demands of the labor market of developed countries like Japan, it will make an important contribution to the country's economy, employment and foreign earnings," Bobby Hajjaj added.
He said necessary policy and institutional initiatives will be taken to further strengthen language education, skill development and quality technical education.
The experiences and recommendations of expatriate Bangladeshis will be considered with importance through coordination with the relevant ministries and agencies, he continued.
Assuring that the issue of ensuring that no talented student misses the opportunity for higher education abroad only due to financial constraints will be given due importance, Bobby Hajjaj said Bangladeshi students studying abroad are important assets for the country.
Their experiences and practical suggestions will play an important role in formulating future policies on education, skill development and human resource formation, he said.
Participants at the meeting emphasized improving the quality of Japanese language education in Bangladesh, introducing a national accreditation system for language education institutions and establishing specialized training institutes for language teachers.
They also called for integrating technical and vocational education and training (TVET) with information technology education.
They also proposed policy support to utilize the skills acquired by young people returning home after training in Japan in the engineering, technology and automotive industries.
Responding to the recommendations, the state minister said the government would work with importance to improve the quality of Japanese language education, formulate a quality control system, enhance teachers' skills and expand technical education suitable for the international labor market.
He also said policy support would be ensured to utilize the knowledge acquired by returning expatriates in the country's industrial and production sectors.
Officials from the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo, Bangladeshi students studying at different universities in Japan, expatriate professionals, businesspeople and community leaders attended the exchange meeting.

CCGP approves procurement of since cargo of LNG from Aramco Trading Singapore
item.description:
The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase (CCGP) on Friday approved the procurement of one cargo of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Aramco Trading Singapore, a fully-owned subsidiary of Saudi Aramco based in Singapore, under a government-to-government (G2G) arrangement to help meet the country’s growing energy demand.
The approval came at the eighth meeting of the CCGP for the 2026-27 fiscal year, held virtually with Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury in the chair on the weekly holiday.
The committee approved the proposal to purchase one LNG cargo from Aramco Trading Singapore for delivery on August 11-12, 2026 through the direct procurement method under the G2G framework.
The LNG will be purchased at a price of $21.55 per MMBtu, according to officials.
However, the committee again did not consider another proposal relating to a long-term LNG procurement arrangement with Gunvor USA LLC.
The Energy and Mineral Resources Division withdrew its proposal, like the Thursday meeting seeking approval for the direct purchase of LNG from Gunvor USA LLC under a G2G arrangement for the period from 2026 to 2038, before it could be placed for the committee’s consideration.
Bangladesh has been importing LNG to supplement declining domestic natural gas production and ensure a stable supply of fuel for power generation and industrial use.
The latest approval is expected to support the country’s gas supply by facilitating timely delivery of an LNG cargo during August.
The country's gas supply is gradually returning to normal after the partial restoration of the Excelerate Energy-operated floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) at Maheshkhali, easing a nationwide shortage that disrupted power generation, industries, CNG stations and household cooking for more than two weeks.
The crisis began on July 21 when a fire damaged the FSRU’s boiler-related electrical systems, forcing the suspension of LNG regasification from one of the country’s two floating LNG terminals.
The outage cut around 450 million cubic feet of gas per day from the national grid, significantly affecting electricity production and industrial operations.
Following repair work by local and foreign engineers, the terminal has resumed partial operations, supplying about 115 million cubic feet of gas per day, with output expected to increase in phases.
Energy Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood on Thursday said gas supply should return to normal within two to three days as repairs continue.
Bangladesh currently faces a daily gas demand of about 3,800 to 4,000 million cubic feet against supply of roughly 2,600 million cubic feet, making imported LNG crucial to meeting domestic demand.
The latest disruption has once again highlighted the country’s growing dependence on LNG imports and the vulnerability of its gas supply system to disruptions at a single FSRU.

item.title: Long queues persist at Dhaka CNG stations amid gas supply woes
item.description:
Long queues of vehicles persisted at compressed natural gas (CNG) filling stations across the capital on Friday as gas supply remained unstable, forcing drivers to wait for hours to refuel.
The prolonged shortage, driven by inadequate pipeline pressure and irregular gas supply, has left CNG auto-rickshaws, buses and private cars lining up at filling stations around the clock, disrupting transport services and causing widespread inconvenience to commuters.
After visiting filling stations in Mohakhali, Tejgaon, Kallyanpur, Shyamoli and Gabtoli, it was found that gas shortages continue across the city. Stations resume dispensing gas when supply is restored but are forced to suspend operations once it runs out. Gas supplied overnight lasted until early morning at some stations, but many had no supply after that.
The shortage has also disrupted public transport, as buses and CNG-powered vehicles remain stranded in long queues at filling stations. Commuters, particularly on working days, are struggling to find transport for office and other essential travel. Many have been forced to walk long distances or pay higher fares for alternative transport.
"We received gas around 9:30pm and started dispensing it immediately. But since dawn, there has been no gas in the line," said Tarique, a sales employee at Akij CNG Filling Station in Tejgaon.
Filling station operators attributed the crisis to inadequate gas supply from the national grid and low pipeline pressure, saying the lack of pressure prevents them from operating compressors efficiently and safely. As a result, they are able to serve only about half the usual number of vehicles.
The shortage has also disrupted public transport, as buses and CNG-powered vehicles remain stranded in long queues at filling stations. Commuters, particularly on working days, are struggling to find transport for office and other essential travel. The ongoing gas crisis continues to take a heavy toll on daily life, affecting both transport services and household expenses. Drivers and vehicle owners urged the authorities to restore adequate gas supply and ensure sufficient pipeline pressure at CNG filling stations without delay.

item.title: Trump signs new orders restricting birthright citizenship
item.description:
US President Donald Trump dismissed a previous Supreme Court decision on citizenship as “very unfortunate” while signing two new executive orders restricting birthright citizenship on Thursday.
“It was close, but a very, very unfortunate decision,” Trump said of the 6-3 vote top court ruling two months ago.
The ruling rebuked Trump’s previous attempt to challenge the constitutional provision that allows individuals born on US soil automatic citizenship.
Birthright citizenship is enshrined in the 14th ​Amendment of the US Constitution. The rule guarantees citizenship for babies born in the US with only narrow exceptions, such as the children of foreign diplomats or members of an enemy occupying force.
“This was done for a different reason. This ​was done right after the Civil War. This ‌was for the babies of slaves, and what’s happening now?” Trump said on Thursday.
Trump’s close advisor and the architect of his immigration policy, Stephen Miller, said one of the orders signed Thursday seeks to deny birthright citizenship to children of members of “foreign terrorist organizations” as well as “large categories of people who lobby and act on behalf of foreign governments.”
Miller added that the order “ensures that large numbers of people who wrongly (would) be getting birthright citizenship will no longer be eligible for those benefits.”
The second executive order targets what Trump called “birth tourism.” The expression refers to visitors securing visas and traveling to the US so they would give birth while in the country, so their children are entitled to US citizenship.
“That practice of birth tourism is, as of ​the signing of this order, hereby banned. What that means is that no one in the world is anymore allowed to obtain a ​visa for this ‌fraudulent purpose,” Miller added.
Currently, there are no official figures depicting the number of foreigners who come to the US for the explicit purpose of giving birth to obtain citizenship. But the Trump-aligned Center for Immigration Studies claims that between 20,000-25,000 mothers did so 2016-2017.
The White House has argued that the new executive orders do not fall within the limits of the Supreme Court ruling.
Still, the orders are expected to be challenged in court.
“I thought we were going to win it at the Supreme Court,” Trump said on Thursday. ”Unfortunately, we had a bad decision, very unfair decision. Our country suffers because of it and we’re ending it a different way,” Trump said.
Currently, no US law bans so-called birth tourism, but a federal regulation implemented in 2020 during Trump’s first term prohibits using temporary tourist and business visas for the primary purpose of obtaining US citizenship for a newborn.

item.description:
A former leader of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) allegedly died after falling from the rooftop of a five-storey building while fleeing during a police raid in Savar, on the outskirts of Dhaka, early Friday.
The deceased was identified as Monowarul Hossain Bokshi, 29, a former vice-president of Savar Thana JCD and son of Jafar, a security guard at the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC). The incident occurred around 12:00am at the BPATC Staff Quarters in Savar.
According to police, Shahariar Kabir Soumi had fled from Pirganj in Rangpur with a young woman following a romantic relationship. The woman's family later filed a missing diary with Pirganj Police Station. Acting on the complaint, a team from Pirganj Police arrived at Savar Model Police Station around 11:00pm on Thursday before conducting a joint raid with Savar police at the residence of Monowarul, the suspect's maternal uncle.
Police said Soumi and the woman had already left the house before officers arrived. Sensing the police presence, Monowarul allegedly ran to the rooftop in an attempt to flee. Police followed him to the roof, where he suddenly fell from the five-storey building.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) Saiful Alam of Savar Model Police Station said the Pirganj police had come to Savar to arrest the suspect and informed the local police, who then joined the operation.
"While the Pirganj police entered the building to apprehend the suspect, a young man fell from the rooftop and died. Members of Savar Model Police Station were stationed outside the building," the OC said.
Police have formed a five-member investigation committee to probe the incident.
