Tonu murder: SC scraps bail of ex-Army member Hafizur
item.description:
The Appellate Division’s chamber court on Thursday stayed the High Court's order granting interim bail to former army member Hafizur Rahman, an accused in the murder case of Comilla’s Sohagi Jahan Tonu, and ordered him to surrender within 24 hours.
If Hafizur fails to surrender within the stipulated time, police have been directed to arrest him, Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal said after the hearing.
The order came after the state challenged the High Court's August 2 decision granting Hafizur six months' interim bail.
The High Court bench of Justice Zafar Ahmed and Justice Sathika Hossain had also issued a rule asking why he should not be granted permanent bail and directed the authorities concerned to respond within four weeks.
Following the High Court order, Hafizur was released from jail, prompting the state to move the Appellate Division seeking cancellation of the bail.
Deputy Attorney General Shiuli Khanam and Assistant Attorneys General Sabbir Hossain, Md Mizanur Rahman, Rezaul Karim and Mir Moniruzzaman represented the state, while lawyer Muslem Uddin Bhuiyan appeared for Hafizur.
Hafizur, 52, a former senior warrant officer of the Bangladesh Army, was arrested by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) from his residence in Keraniganj on April 21 in connection with the high-profile murder case.
Tonu, a student and private tutor, went missing on the evening of March 20, 2016, after going to a house inside Comilla Cantonment for a tutoring session. Her body was later recovered from a bush near the cantonment's power house area.
The murder has remained under investigation for years, drawing widespread public attention. Hafizur's arrest earlier this year renewed focus on the long-running case.

item.title: RAB arrests two with rare Sterling submachine gun, foreign pistol in Rajbari raids
item.description:
Members of Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested two alleged armed men and seized a rare foreign-made Sterling submachine gun, a foreign-made pistol and 34 rounds of live ammunition in separate raids in Rajbari's Sadar and Goalanda upazilas.
The arrested men were identified as Md Momin Molla and Hasan Ali Biswas. RAB said they have links to the banned Sarbahara Party's Manju-Jahangir group.
The arrests were made in separate operations conducted by members of RAB-10's CPC-3 Faridpur Camp on Wednesday evening and night, RAB-10 Commanding Officer Additional DIG Md Asaduzzaman told a press conference at the RAB Media Centre in Karwan Bazar on Thursday afternoon.
Company Commander of RAB's Faridpur Camp, Major Farhan Mahmud Moktada, was also present.
Briefing reporters, the Commanding Officer said, acting on a tip-off, its members conducted the first raid at Mahishkhola Mollabari area under Pachuria Union in Rajbari Sadar around 6:45 pm on Wednesday. Momin Molla was arrested during the operation.
RAB recovered a foreign-made Sterling submachine gun, two magazines, 28 rounds of live ammunition and two mobile phones from his possession.
Asaduzzaman said Momin Molla is a Saudi Arabia expatriate who returned to Bangladesh about a month ago and was scheduled to fly back to Saudi Arabia on August 13.
He added that the recovered Sterling submachine gun is an extremely rare type of firearm.
In another operation around 10:15 pm the same day, RAB arrested Hasan Ali Biswas near Jalil Member Bridge in Chhoto Bhakla Union under Goalanda upazila.
During the raid, RAB recovered a foreign-made pistol, one magazine, six rounds of live ammunition, several locally made weapons, four mobile phones and Tk 15,300 in cash from his possession.
The RAB-10 chief said preliminary interrogation revealed that both arrested men have links to the Sarbahara Party, while Hasan Ali Biswas is associated with the party's Manju-Jahangir group.
He said RAB's drive to arrest the group's leader, Manju-Jahangir, is continuing.
He also said local residents had been disturbed by the alleged criminal activities of the arrested men. RAB will seek remand of the accused to identify the source of the weapons, their use and other associates.
RAB said cases under the Arms Act are being filed against the two men with the respective police stations and legal action is underway.

item.title: 'UN withheld July uprising eyewitness identities over death penalty provision'
item.description:
The United Nations did not share the identities of eyewitnesses cited in its fact-finding report on the July 2024 Mass Uprising because Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Act still retains the death penalty, a prosecutor told the tribunal on Thursday.
Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim made the disclosure while presenting arguments before International Crimes Tribunal-2 in a crimes against humanity case against seven leaders of the now-banned Awami League and its affiliated organizations, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader.
During the hearing, Monawar said armed activists of the Chhatra League and Awami League attacked protesters between July 14 and July 17, 2024, on the instructions of senior party leaders, adding that the incidents were documented in the UN's fact-finding report.
He said the report contains references for all witnesses but the UN had informed the prosecution that it would disclose the identities of eyewitnesses only if the death penalty was removed from Bangladesh's ICT law.
"As a result, we did not receive the UN's eyewitnesses," the prosecutor said, adding that the prosecution is instead producing its own eyewitnesses before the tribunal.
Following the fall of the Awami League government during the Jul uprising, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) published a fact-finding report examining events between July 1 and August 15, 2024.
The report held senior leaders of the then-ruling Awami League responsible for atrocities and crimes against humanity committed during the period.
To prepare the report, the UN fact-finding mission conducted investigations in eight cities—Dhaka, Chittagong, Rangpur, Rajshahi, Khulna, Bogra, Sylhet and Gazipur.
It interviewed more than 230 victims and eyewitnesses, along with 36 government officials, members of the security forces and political figures familiar with the events.
Monawar told the tribunal that the UN withheld the identities of those eyewitnesses because the ICT Act still provides for capital punishment. The United Nations has consistently called for the abolition of the death penalty for all crimes.
Besides Obaidul Quader, the accused are Awami League Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, former state minister for Information and Broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat, Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and General Secretary Mainul Hossain Khan, and Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif.
All seven accused are currently absconding.
